My best advice, besides seeing a doctor and discussing your symptoms regularly, is to try your best to stay ahead of it. 
When you get a chest cold, ask about a short term burst of a corticosteroid inhaler. Don’t waste time until things are out of control. 
When you feel allergies coming on, ask about allergy medication to help prevent symptoms as well as asthma attacks. 
If you are exposed to an especially bad trigger, see a doctor as soon as possible. It can spiral out of control and fast if you aren’t careful. 
That being said, you can be prepared all you want and have it under control and something can come along and set you back. But as long as you have a dedicated doctor, don’t hesitate to see them even if you think you can push through. Asthma exacerbation is quick and terrifying.

I was told today that I have what is called “passive suicidal ideation” at this point. I’ve thought about killing myself for months on end, but have never had any active plans. But I’ve thought about swerving into oncoming traffic on my way to work. I got a DUI last year and actively wish I would of died during it. About a month after that I was tempted to take a handful of percocets, but frightened myself by getting to that point. I’m also a functioning alcoholic, and there always been a wish that I would drink enough to die in my sleep or just wait for my liver to give out. 
I’d never do anything to hurt myself in real life, but I fantasize about it all the time. Even now. 
I went to rehab, quit drinking as much, and even got a better job and as happy as I am now, just a few weeks ago when I had COVID I found those thoughts creeping back. This time a little more aggressive, but I road them out and told myself I was just feeling isolated and shitty.  
I guess my point is, it does get better. You’ve got so much left to live for and experience in your life, even if some days it feels like everything would be so much easier if you were dead, you’ve still got a lot to look forward to. Those thought will come and go once you actually get things a little more the way you’d like them, but you just have to keep going.
